arxiv-2203-07588.title: When Cell-Free Massive MIMO Meets OTFS Modulation: The Downlink Case
arxiv-2203-07588.creator: Mohammadali Mohammadi, Hien Quoc Ngo, Michail Matthaiou
arxiv-2203-07588.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mohammadali Mohammadi, Hien Quoc Ngo, Michail Matthaiou. We provide a performance evaluation of orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation in cell-free massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) systems. By leveraging the inherent sparsity of the delay-Doppler (DD) representation of time-varying channels, we apply the embedded pilot-aided channel estimation method with reduced guard intervals and derive the minimum mean-square error estimate of the channel gains from received uplink pilots at the access points (APs). Each AP applies conjugate beamforming to transmit data to the users.

arxiv-2502-04217.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wei Kuang, Vishwas Rao, Alexis Montoison, François Pacaud, Mihai Anitescu. We propose a method to recover the sparse discrete Fourier transform (DFT) of a signal that is both noisy and potentially incomplete, with missing values. The problem is formulated as a penalized least-squares minimization based on the inverse discrete Fourier transform (IDFT) with an ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -penalty term, reformulated to be solvable using a primal-dual interior point method (IPM).

arxiv-2507-22209.creator: Christian Clark, Byung-Doh Oh, William Schuler
arxiv-2507-22209.description: Abstract Contextual entropy is a psycholinguistic measure capturing the anticipated difficulty of processing a word just before it is encountered. For convenience, entropy is typically estimated based on a language model’s probability distribution over a word’s first subword token.

uslaw-usc-t18-s2259a.title: 18 U.S.C. § 2259A — Assessments in child pornography cases
uslaw-usc-t18-s2259a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s2259a.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 110 (Sexual Exploitation And Other Abuse Of Children). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— In addition to any other criminal penalty, restitution, or special assessment authorized by law, the court shall assess— (1) not more than $17,000 on any person convicted of an offense under section 2252(a)(4).
